committees.name: Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee

dimensions.assessment: Affects institutions of higher education receiving or seeking DHS funding and students or researchers at those institutions.
dimensions.evidence: an institution of higher education... which has a relationship with a Confucius Institute, Thousand Talents Program, or Chinese entity of concern is ineligible to receive any funds from the Department of Homeland Security

dimensions.assessment: Denies all DHS funding to non-compliant institutions unless they terminate specified relationships or obtain a waiver.
dimensions.evidence: is ineligible to receive any funds from the Department of Homeland Security, unless the institution terminates the relationship

dimensions.assessment: Restricts the flow of DHS grant and research funds to affected universities, though the total dollar volume is not specified.
Establishes broad funding disqualifications, waiver protocols involving the Director of National Intelligence, and mandatory annual reporting.
dimensions.evidence: To establish Department of Homeland Security funding restrictions on institutions of higher education that have a relationship with Confucius Institutes, and for other purposes.

dimensions.assessment: Permanent funding restriction taking effect 12 months after enactment, with annual reporting and renewable waiver provisions.
dimensions.evidence: Beginning with the first fiscal year that begins after the date that is 12 months after the date of the enactment of this Act

missing_information: Total dollar amount of DHS funds currently received by institutions with such relationships
importance_detail.rationale: The bill restricts Department of Homeland Security funding to institutions of higher education that maintain relationships with Confucius Institutes, the Thousand Talents Program, or specified Chinese entities of concern, subject to waiver provisions.
